channel.title: Teppei Nakano — Reading notes
channel.description: One takeaway per paper for local LLMs and medical ML

item.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
item.description: The middle of a long context is unused. RAG either puts evidence at the ends or shortens the context.

item.title: The shaky foundations of large language models and foundation models for electronic health records
item.description: Before the task name, I check whether EHR foundation-model labels are billing or annotation, and whether the split is by patient.

item.title: Large language models encode clinical knowledge
item.description: A board-exam score is not faithfulness to a ward protocol. A medical LLM decides citations and what it will not emit first.

item.title: AI for radiographic COVID-19 detection selects shortcuts over signal
item.description: Imaging models pick laterality markers and site style before disease. Before saliency, I ask whether the embedding predicts the hospital.

item.title: Do We Still Need Clinical Language Models?
item.description: A general LLM can win a clinical task and still be unusable if notes cannot leave. The boundary precedes the model name.

item.title: Variable generalization performance of a deep learning model to detect pneumonia in chest radiographs
item.description: In-hospital AUROC dies next door. I read pneumonia papers for scanner and protocol text before the leaderboard.

item.title: Capabilities of GPT-4 on Medical Challenge Problems
item.description: A challenge-problem score is not EHR input and not an accountability story. I read it as an upper bound on a demo.

item.title: Dissecting racial bias in an algorithm used to manage the health of populations
item.description: Cost as a proxy for risk learns access. I write what the teacher stands in for before I write the loss.

item.title: GatorTron: A Large Clinical Language Model to Unlock Patient Information from Unstructured Electronic Health Records
item.description: The point of a large clinical LM is notes trained inside the institution. I look at weight release and the teacher first.

item.title: The myth of generalisability in clinical research and machine learning in health care
item.description: Generalisation is a report of which shifts you survived, not a property. I do not call a single AUROC generalisable.

item.title: Publicly Available Clinical BERT Embeddings
item.description: Public clinical BERT leans toward MIMIC prose. I do not freeze the embedding without a local-note re-eval.

item.title: Scalable and accurate deep learning with electronic health records
item.description: Ingesting the EHR as a sequence is not the result. The result is whether anything after time t leaked in.

item.title: BioBERT: a pre-trained biomedical language representation model for biomedical text mining
item.description: BERT on PubMed. That is paper English, not a ward note. I do not confuse corpora by name.

item.title: MIMIC-III, a freely accessible critical care database
item.description: The default public ICU set. I read which MIMIC version, whether patients collide, and whether clocks agree.

item.title: Hidden stratification causes clinically meaningful failures in machine learning for medical imaging
item.description: Rare subtypes sink under mean AUROC. If the stratum is not a label, the mean hides it.

item.title: CheXpert: A Large Chest Radiograph Dataset with Uncertainty Labels and Expert Comparison
item.description: The uncertain label (pos / uncertain / neg) is the dataset. Collapse it to positive and the model never learns radiologist doubt.

item.title: MIMIC-CXR, a de-identified publicly available database of chest radiographs with free-text reports
item.description: A public set with images and reports. Split by patient. Do not mix acquisition time and report time.

item.title: The Precision-Recall Plot Is More Informative than the ROC Plot When Evaluating Binary Classifiers on Imbalanced Datasets
item.description: On imbalance, PR comes first. AUROC can look high while almost every page is a miss.

item.title: Underdiagnosis bias of artificial intelligence algorithms applied to chest radiographs in under-served patient populations
item.description: Under mean AUROC, false negatives rise in under-served groups. I do not ship a chest model I cannot slice.

item.title: Tackling the widespread and critical impact of batch effects in high-throughput data
item.description: Batch can outrun biology. I put a cross-study split before the correction.

item.title: Deep learning predicts hip fracture using confounding patient and healthcare variables
item.description: It looks like fracture and is hospital and scanner. I plot confounders before I print accuracy.

item.title: Adjusting batch effects in microarray expression data using empirical Bayes methods
item.description: ComBat shrinks batch mean and variance. Re-estimating on the test study leaks the evaluation.

item.title: Transparent Reporting of a multivariable prediction model for Individual Prognosis or Diagnosis (TRIPOD)
item.description: Reporting items come first. A paper without split, calibration, and population cannot be reproduced.

item.title: A simple algorithm for identifying negated findings and diseases in discharge summaries
item.description: Half of clinical text is absence. Extraction that ignores negation doubles the findings.

item.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
item.description: Contiguous KV leaves holes. Paging the cache is how the same VRAM holds a batch.

item.title: Decision Curve Analysis: A Novel Method for Evaluating Prediction Models
item.description: Plot net benefit against the treat / do-not-treat threshold. A high AUROC that loses at the operating threshold does not ship.

item.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
item.description: Attention is slow from HBM traffic, not from approximation. Tile it; keep it exact.

item.title: Multitask learning and benchmarking with clinical time series data
item.description: The MIMIC benchmark is the task definition and the split. I do not silently copy that preprocessing onto my own task.

item.title: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints
item.description: Sharing K/V heads cuts KV bytes before it cuts quality. That is the local-inference estimate.

item.title: Do no harm: a roadmap for responsible machine learning for health care
item.description: Responsibility is who can stop it, not a model card. I write the off-switch before deployment.

item.title: RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding
item.description: Positions are rotated, not added. Relative offset enters the dot product. Long-context work is about those periods.

item.title: The false hope of current approaches to explainable artificial intelligence in health care
item.description: Saliency is not evidence of generalization. I print external-site and slice failures before an explanation figure.

item.title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
item.description: A sliding window breaks unless you keep the first tokens. The sink is a lemma of the window.

item.title: Moderated estimation of fold change and dispersion for RNA-seq data with DESeq2
item.description: Shrink dispersion, then test a difference. I do not hand raw counts to a learner.

item.title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
item.description: A small model drafts; the large one verifies. Wall time shrinks only when rejects stay rare.

item.title: Fast, sensitive and accurate integration of single-cell data with Harmony
item.description: Integration pulls batches together and should leave biology. I do not put the test study into the integration fit.

item.title: LLM.int8(): 8-bit Matrix Multiplication for Transformers at Scale
item.description: Even at 8-bit, outlier channels stay in 16-bit. Quantization is not a uniform shave.

item.title: Current best practices in single-cell RNA-seq analysis: a tutorial
item.description: In single-cell, the preprocessing order is the result. I freeze QC, normalize, integrate, cluster before the learner.

item.title: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration
item.description: Weight importance follows activation magnitude. MSE alone drops the channels you needed.

item.title: Characterizing genetic intra-tumor heterogeneity in 500 tumors from 38 tissues
item.description: One biopsy is a piece of the tumor. I split heterogeneity into diversity inside the sample and extrapolation to unsampled regions.

item.title: MIMIC-IV, a freely accessible electronic health record dataset
item.description: The successor to III. Write version and module. Do not silently reuse III preprocessing on IV.

item.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
item.description: Add a low-rank delta. Choose which matrices before you choose rank.

item.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized Language Models
item.description: Add LoRA while the base sits in 4-bit. Close to the air-gapped default when full finetune VRAM is gone.

item.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
item.description: Given preference pairs, you can update the policy without a reward model. Pair quality precedes the loss.

item.title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers
item.description: Quantize weights with no training. Calibration text precedes the bit width.

item.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
item.description: SFT, then reinforce from human preference. The template for “aligning” a local stack.

item.title: FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning
item.description: On top of FA1’s IO cut, fix how work is partitioned. I check this is the default kernel before I talk about approximating attention.

item.title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
item.description: Each token picks one expert. Compute is sparse; memory still pays for every expert.

item.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
item.description: Retrieve before you generate. Do not bake the knowledge into weights. Score retrieval and generation apart.

item.title: Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head is All You Need
item.description: One K/V head slashes KV bytes. The prehistory of GQA. I write the quality trade next to the memory estimate.

item.title: Train Short, Test Long: Attention with Linear Biases Enables Input Length Extrapolation
item.description: Add a linear bias on distance. A different path to length extrapolation than RoPE. I do not mix the recipes.

item.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
item.description: Put questions and passages in one space. Before dropping BM25, I look at what dense retrieval catches and drops.

item.title: YaRN: Efficient Context Window Extension of Large Language Models
item.description: Stretch RoPE frequencies by band. In operations I try this before raising the base in one shot.

item.title: Attention Is All You Need
item.description: Drop recurrence; make distance constant with attention. Current decoders keep one side of this paper.

item.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
item.description: For a fixed compute budget, more tokens beat an oversized model. I use it to size an air-gapped pretrain.

item.title: Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization
item.description: Decouple decay from the gradient. That is not Adam plus L2. Leave Norm γ out of decay.

item.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
item.description: Loss falls as a power of size, data, and compute. The optimal split was revised later by Chinchilla.

item.title: Root Mean Square Layer Normalization
item.description: No mean subtraction; divide by RMS. With pre-norm, that is current decoder normalization.

item.title: ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models
item.description: Shard optimizer state across GPUs. Whether an air-gapped train fits is the ZeRO stage, not the parameter count.

item.title: On Layer Normalization in the Transformer Architecture
item.description: Pre-norm leaves the residual as an identity. That is one reason a deep decoder trains.

item.title: The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration
item.description: Argmax loops. Temperature is not enough. Cut the tail with a nucleus (top-p).

item.title: Mixed Precision Training
item.description: Compute in FP16; keep an FP32 copy for stability. I do not mix this with inference quantization.

item.title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
item.description: Late interaction over tokens. Higher than one vector, heavier to store. A middle option for internal search.

item.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
item.description: Move the shape of the teacher’s logits, with a temperature. Relations survive better than hard labels.

item.title: Leveraging Passage Retrieval with Generative Models for Open Domain Question Answering
item.description: Encode passages separately; fuse in the decoder. Attribution is easier than one long concatenated prompt.

item.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
item.description: Deeper, stronger nets are worse calibrated. I put ECE and temperature scaling next to AUROC.

item.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
item.description: LLM judges are biased by position and self-preference. A partial substitute for humans, not the only KPI.

item.title: Representation Learning with Contrastive Predictive Coding
item.description: Pick the positive out of noise. InfoNCE became the name of that loss.

item.title: Training a Helpful and Harmless Assistant with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
item.description: Helpful and harmless do not rise on one reward. I write which preference the data prioritized.

item.title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units
item.description: Split rare words into subwords. The tokenizer is part of the model, not preprocessing.

item.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
item.description: Write a constitution first; let the model critique itself. That cuts human pairs. RLHF without principles becomes a department’s taste.

item.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
item.description: In-context examples steer without a weight update. Demos are strong and weak to contamination and secret exemplars.

item.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
item.description: A bidirectional understanding model. Masking and KV growth are not a decoder’s. I do not mix the names.

item.title: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding
item.description: A broad multiple-choice set is both a contamination risk and a poor proxy for the floor task. Not the only hiring number.

item.title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
item.description: A public-weight starting point for an air gap. I read the license and the chat post-train recipe before the pretrain story.

item.title: Mistral 7B
item.description: GQA and a sliding window make 7B cheaper. One comparison point for a small air-gapped model.

item.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
item.description: Writing intermediate steps helps arithmetic and logic. In medicine a hallucinated procedure can still look well-formed.

item.title: GLU Variants Improve Transformer
item.description: Gate the FFN. Llama-family MLPs are this line. I do not borrow a ReLU-FFN learning rate.

item.title: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
item.description: Unit tests passing is the code-generation eval. Internally those tests can be the secret.
